title: 'It ends here tonight': Billy Shea threatened to kill Peterborough police officers
subtitle: The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has cleared the Peterborough Police Service of any wrongdoing in the fatal shooting of Billy Shea.
article: The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has cleared the Peterborough Police Service of any wrongdoing in the fatal shooting of Billy Shea.

Shea, 27, was shot and killed by police on July 23, 2019 after a police chase that started in Millbrook and ended with a standoff on the Highway 7/115 northbound off-ramp near the The Parkway and Sir Sandford Fleming Drive intersection.

"The Director of the Special Investigations Unit, Joseph Martino, has determined there is no basis for proceeding with criminal charges in this case, and the file is closed," the SIU states in a press release.
Officers observed a stolen red Mustang in Millbrook around 8:35 p.m. Tuesday and followed the car to the intersection.

The standoff began following the collision. It involved heavily armed police and an armed man in the stolen car. Officers approached the vehicle and an interaction ensued between them and Shea, the SIU said.
One officer discharged his firearm and Shea was struck, the SIU said. Shea was taken by paramedics under police escort to Peterborough Regional Health Centre where he was pronounced dead.
Shea was a federal parolee wanted for an armed robbery in Hamilton, according to Hamilton Police and the OPP.
According to the SIU decision, over the course of almost one hour, an officer attempted to convince Shea to drop his firearm and exit the vehicle.

The SIU reports that Shea made officers aware that he was in possession of a triple barrel shotgun. A woman in the car also inadvertently dropped a handgun outside the vehicle. The report states Shea repeatedly indicated he was going to kill himself or, alternatively, that he wanted police to shoot him. He also stated he wanted to die but that he did not have the nerve to do it himself, threatening to kill police if they didn't kill him.
According to the SIU, on multiple occasions Shea said words to the effect, "It ends here tonight, it's over, I am not going back to jail."

He also repeatedly pointed the barrel of the shotgun under his chin, according to the report. After about 45 minutes of negotiations, Shea stood up in the car and indicated that the magic mushrooms he had previously consumed were beginning to take effect.

A message went over the police radios to all officers present that there was risk of crossfire due to the location of various officers around the subject car. A Peterborough police officer was designated to take the shot if Shea were to leave the vehicle. With the shotgun positioned under his chin, Shea swung one leg over the driver's door and straddled it while an officer continued to plead with him to stay inside the vehicle. Shea then turned the gun on the woman in the vehicle before he swung his other leg out the car.

"With his left hand holding the barrel of the shotgun under his chin and his right on the trigger, he turned to his right side and moved the barrel forward and away from his chin, bringing the stock back and in a position to discharge the firearm away from himself," the SIU decision reads.

At that point, Shea began to walk away from the car toward three police officers, causing the designated officer to believe the officers were now at risk. The officer discharged his rifle twice, shooting Shea twice in the back.

"In the subject officer's interview with SIU investigators, he indicated that when Complainant #1 (Shea) exited the Mustang with the firearm, he feared for the life of his fellow officers, as well as his own; this fear appears to have been shared by the other officers present," SIU director Joseph Martino wrote in his decision.
